cells.tense: You are at the table with the pen and the old thing is breathing.
cells.act: rebalance by small corrections, not a lurch
cells.ask: Take one piece of what you hand on that's gone stiff — a word, a timing, a small yes — and shift it by a degree, then leave it. No rebuild.
cells.core:
You can pass something down without turning it into a rule. The story, the recipe, the way your people do a thing — you carry it and it shifts as the people shift. Nobody has to sign anything to belong, and that is how it should run: the thing stays alive because the one carrying it stays near the ones it's for.

What bends it now is speed. You can feel the shape moving and you keep reaching to correct all of it at once. Try the smaller move. Choose a single piece of what you carry and adjust it by a degree — a phrasing, a timing, a small yes or no — then let it sit. You don't have to fix the whole line in one motion. Small turns keep a thing alive; a lurch makes people set it down.
cells.sheetLine: You carry what matters and it moves as the people do.
cells.verb: carrying what's worth keeping across the gap to whoever comes next
cells.place: where the false structure comes down on its own and the clearing is what's left

cells.tense: You will be guarding the form against the people it was made for.
cells.act: let one structure collapse that could not hold
cells.ask: Name a form you're propping that the ones it was for have already walked past, and stop holding it up — let it come down, then look at what stands.
cells.core:
You know what the transmission is for, and the coming days have you defending its letter. The version you learned gets treated as the only valid one; the ones who'd carry it forward get measured against a shape they didn't grow in. Belonging starts depending on conformity, and the windows close. What was built to carry meaning across the gap now stands between you and the ones on the far side of it.

Here is the move that clears it: let one form go — not the meaning behind it, the form. The one you're propping that the ones it was for have already walked past. Stop holding it up. Let it come down.

That is not a loss. It's what this place is for.

cells.tense: You were building from scratch what others were already carrying.
cells.act: step back far enough to see the whole arrangement
cells.ask: Stop rebuilding this alone and look at the whole arrangement — sketch its shape in a few lines and name what's already being carried by others.
cells.core:
Where meaning gets passed across time, you've been starting from zero. No shared framework holds, so every question is yours to answer new. It gets lonely, and the loneliness is intelligent — you can see how a thing works underneath. But the sight stays private, and what you build doesn't connect to what came before or to anyone building beside you.

The route back is not to push harder into the bare spot. Stand farther off from what you're rebuilding by yourself and take in the whole arrangement — what's already here, what shape it makes, what others have done with the same problem. Draw it without the details, in a few lines. That kind of sight is what a framework is made of. You don't have to reinvent the wheel if you can find one.
cells.sheetLine: You start from zero and miss what's already being carried.

cells.tense: You are already carrying meaning to others while saying you don't.
cells.act: find the centre and hold it while things move
cells.ask: The next time something you do lands with someone and they take it up, stay in the middle of it while the moment moves — adjust by a little and watch it go with them.
cells.core:
Something comes off you and stays with them. A phrase, a way of handling a thing, a story they repeat without remembering where they got it. That is what this stretch of you does, and it has been doing it through you for a long while. Your account of it is that you stay clear of all that. The account is wrong, and the ones near you have not been confused about it for a minute.

There is a simpler version of the same work, and it is not to announce yourself. It is to stay near the middle of it while it happens. The next time something you do lands with someone and they take it up, hold the centre of it, adjust by a hair, and watch it go with them. Not a lecture, not a lesson. The work stays yours, held by its own doer.
cells.sheetLine: You're already the teacher. You just don't count it.

attempts.check: The record supports the card, the seat, the tense, and the mechanism, but I nearly wrote that the person is 'already teaching' as if it were a fact of their history rather than a description of what the capacity is doing right now; the reader could reasonably say 'I'm not a teacher, I just know some things.' The asks survive that objection: each is small, self-contained, and teachers nothing beyond the doing of it. The sentence that serves me rather than them is any line that admires the pattern I invented; I kept those out and left the mechanism plain.
